ABSTRACT
Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation
models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geomet-
ric priors.
However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene
dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution
harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry represen-
tation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from
camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-
view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder

queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future
scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states
can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras,
while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-

INTRODUCTION
Learning to predict how the physical world evolves is a central goal of world modeling (Ha &
Schmidhuber, 2018), with direct relevance to autonomous driving, robotics, and embodied intelli-

Learning to predict how the physical world evolves is a central goal of world modeling (Ha &
Schmidhuber, 2018), with direct relevance to autonomous driving, robotics, and embodied intelli-
gence. Visual world models predict the future in pixel space (Hu et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024b;
Gao et al., 2024; NVIDIA et al., 2025), which can introduce substantial representational redundancy
and make geometric consistency difficult to maintain. This has motivated increasing interest in 3D
world models, which represent and predict future environments in geometrically grounded state
spaces. By explicitly encoding spatial structure and 3D relationships, these representations provide
a structured and geometrically grounded state space that more directly reflects the real world.
Recent 3D world models have explored a range of structured geometric state spaces, including
depth, occupancy, point-based representations, and 3D Gaussians (Zheng et al., 2024; Zhang et al.,

Recent 3D world models have explored a range of structured geometric state spaces, including
depth, occupancy, point-based representations, and 3D Gaussians (Zheng et al., 2024; Zhang et al.,
2024; Yang et al., 2024; Zhu et al., 2025; Chen et al., 2025; Zuo et al., 2025). In parallel, geometry
foundation models (GFMs) have substantially advanced feed-forward 3D perception by learning rich
geometric representations directly from RGB observations (Wang et al., 2024a; Yang et al., 2025;
Wang et al., 2025b;a; 2026). Benefiting from large-scale pretraining, these representations capture
strong geometric priors that generalize across scenes and tasks, making them attractive state spaces
for predictive world modeling. Building on this capability, recent approaches have begun to directly
model temporal evolution in pretrained geometry feature spaces (Sun et al., 2026; Lu et al., 2026). In
particular, VGGT-World (Sun et al., 2026) treats frozen VGGT features as world states and predicts

particular, VGGT-World (Sun et al., 2026) treats frozen VGGT features as world states and predicts
their future evolution, demonstrating the potential of GFM representations for 3D forecasting.
Despite the strong performance achieved by recent GFM-based 3D world models, a strong repre-
sentation for geometric perception is not necessarily an appropriate state representation for world

so changes in camera viewpoint can induce substantial changes in the representation even when the
underlying physical scene remains unchanged. When such features are directly used as predictive
states, a temporal model would account simultaneously for genuine scene evolution and camera-
induced variation, although these arise from fundamentally different sources. In particular, even
a static scene can undergo substantial changes in feature space as the camera moves, forcing the
temporal model to predict viewpoint-dependent transformations that do not correspond to physical
scene evolution. This unnecessary variation makes the latent dynamics more complex and therefore
harder to predict over long horizons. FR3D (Morbitzer et al., 2026) also shows that separating ego-
motion from scene forecasting can improve temporal modeling, but its predictive state still inherits

the view-dependent structure of the underlying reconstruction representation. We argue that such
separation should instead be built into the representation itself: the state should describe what the
world is, while the camera should determine only how that world is observed.
To this end, we introduce GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry state learned from pretrained GFM
features. Given multi-view observations, a scene tokenizer compresses their geometry features into a
compact scene state represented in a shared scene coordinate system, while the query viewpoint is in-
troduced only during decoding. Specifically, a geometry decoder takes the scene state together with
rays from a query camera and predicts the geometry observed from that viewpoint. Consequently,
the same scene state can be queried repeatedly from different viewpoints without re-encoding the

rays from a query camera and predicts the geometry observed from that viewpoint. Consequently,
the same scene state can be queried repeatedly from different viewpoints without re-encoding the
scene. This transforms view-conditioned GFM features into a representation in which scene geom-
etry is explicitly separated from camera-dependent observation.
Building on this representation, we formulate 3D world modeling directly in the scene-state space.
The temporal model can therefore focus solely on predicting scene dynamics, while camera evo-
lution is modeled independently. At inference time, a predicted future state can be decoded using
either a separately predicted camera trajectory or a user-controlled camera. Our formulation also
maintains a consistent scene gauge throughout temporal prediction and geometry decoding, avoid-
ing the need for per-frame scale alignment during rollout.

We evaluate our approach on large-scale dynamic driving scenes, using Waymo (Sun et al., 2020) for
in-domain evaluation and KITTI (Geiger et al., 2012) and nuScenes (Caesar et al., 2020) for zero-
shot transfer. Our approach outperforms the compared world models in depth forecasting across all
reported horizons, while maintaining a consistent scale throughout the forecasting rollout. Experi-
ments further demonstrate geometrically consistent querying across viewpoints and generalization
across driving datasets. Ablation results show that view decoupling makes the scene representation
more predictable. Together, these findings support view-decoupled geometry states derived from
pretrained GFMs as an effective representation for predictive 3D world modeling.
Our contributions are threefold:
• We identify viewpoint coupling in geometry foundation model features as a limitation when

Our contributions are threefold:
• We identify viewpoint coupling in geometry foundation model features as a limitation when
using them as predictive world states, and introduce GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry
state derived from pretrained GFM representations that separates scene content from how
the scene is observed.
• We develop a scene-state learning framework that realizes GeoState through a Scene To-
kenizer that aggregates multi-view GFM features into a shared scene state and a query-
conditioned Geometry Decoder that introduces the query viewpoint only at decoding time.
• We formulate a 3D world model that predicts scene evolution directly in GeoState space
while modeling camera evolution separately, and demonstrate long-horizon geometry fore-
casting, geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and zero-shot generalization across
driving datasets without per-frame scale alignment.

RELATED WORK
2.1
3D WORLD MODELS
Recent world models increasingly move beyond pixel-space prediction toward structured 3D scene
modeling and forecasting. Copilot4D (Zhang et al., 2024) and ViDAR (Yang et al., 2024) forecast
future point clouds, while OccWorld (Zheng et al., 2024) and DOME (Gu et al., 2024) predict scene

evolution in semantic occupancy space. DIO (Diehl et al., 2025) represents future scene geometry
and motion through decomposable implicit occupancy-flow fields, and GaussianWorld (Zuo et al.,
2025) models scene evolution in 3D Gaussian space for streaming occupancy prediction. More re-
cently, several approaches directly use learned geometry representations as predictive world states.
VGGT-World (Sun et al., 2026) forecasts future VGGT features, while GeoWAM (Lu et al., 2026)
learns geometry-aware predictive states for autonomous driving. FR3D (Morbitzer et al., 2026) pre-
dicts the latent state of a pretrained 3D reconstruction model while modeling ego-motion separately.
In contrast, we remove viewpoint dependence from the geometry state itself and introduce viewpoint
only as a query condition during decoding.

GEOMETRY FOUNDATION MODELS
Geometry foundation models provide strong pretrained priors for multi-view 3D perception.
DUSt3R (Wang et al., 2024a) formulates reconstruction through pointmap prediction, while
Fast3R (Yang et al., 2025) scales joint reconstruction to larger collections of views. CUT3R (Wang
et al., 2025b) introduces a persistent latent state for continuously integrating observations, and
VGGT (Wang et al., 2025a) unifies camera estimation, depth, point maps, and tracking in a feed-
forward architecture. VGGT-Ω(Wang et al., 2026) further strengthens this paradigm for dynamic
3D scenes, making it a natural geometry backbone for our setting. We build on its pretrained ge-
ometric features and reformulate them into a compact, view-decoupled scene-level representation
better suited for temporal world modeling.

2.3
COMPACT 3D REPRESENTATIONS
A related line of work compresses multi-view observations into compact scene representations.
LVSM (Jin et al., 2025) encodes input views into a fixed-length set of latent tokens for novel-
view synthesis, while Surflo (Gu´edon et al., 2026) aggregates dense VGGT features into a fixed-size
global latent representation for efficient 3D surface reconstruction. 3DRAE (Wei et al., 2026) further
learns a fixed-length, view-decoupled 3D latent space that can be queried from arbitrary cameras.
These works demonstrate that multi-view observations can be represented without retaining a sep-
arate dense representation for each view. While they focus primarily on static scene reconstruction
or novel-view synthesis, our work investigates whether such scene-level representations can serve

arate dense representation for each view. While they focus primarily on static scene reconstruction
or novel-view synthesis, our work investigates whether such scene-level representations can serve
as predictive states for temporal world modeling.

CONCLUSION
We presented GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry state learned from GFM features for predictive
3D world modeling. By separating scene evolution from camera-dependent observation, GeoState
provides a scene representation that can be predicted more effectively over time and queried from
different viewpoints. Future work may extend this framework to embodied settings, where predictive
scene states could support perception, planning, and interaction in dynamic environments.
